title: Access, permissions, RLS/FLS, write-path guards

items.title: Row-level security: restricted member sees only their rows; admin sees all
personas: admin (first sign-in dev admin, platform posture)
two plain members (everyone baseline = showcase_member_default only)

requires: showcase_private_note (OWD private, member_default grants create/read/edit)
two fresh sign-ups, e.g. rls-a@verify.test / rls-b@verify.test
knownGaps: acceptance[5]'s D11 spot-check can be scored only by a runner holding the PRIVATE D11 write-up and its private fix card (maintainer-held, #7463 ruling). The environment this leg needs is that maintainer channel; no public run record, CI job or checkout carries it, by design. Without it, score the D11 spot-check blocked(dependency) (QA run #21720, parked on #22017 row 11), and still score the clause's other half, every skipped object in the verify report explained by its detail line, which needs nothing private. Never restate the defect to justify the verdict

steps: boot showcase isolated (own port + file DB per dogfood skill §0); sign in as admin; sign up members A and B (fresh emails; invite each one first — the stock showcase declares no auth.audience, so the invite_only default answers an uninvited POST /api/v1/auth/sign-up/email 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED; an admin POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member for the address admits the sign-up (or admin POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user, which answers mustChangePassword:true)) — both hold only the everyone baseline showcase_member_default
as A: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note {"title": "A note 1"} and a second note; as B: POST one note — capture the returned ids
as A: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note (list); as B: same; capture both record sets
as A: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<B's id> (foreign by-id read); as A: PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<B's id> {"body": "forged"} (foreign by-id write)
as admin: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note and confirm the full row set (A's + B's rows) is visible — the entitled side of the gate
re-read B's note as admin and confirm the forged PATCH left it byte-identical

run the app-agnostic sweep: runRlsProofs from @objectstack/verify over every showcase object; capture the per-object verdicts. ⚠️ The invocation is `objectstack verify --rls` — the flag is load-bearing: verify.ts declares rls: Flags.boolean({ default: false }) and both the proofs and their report sit behind if (flags.rls), so a BARE `objectstack verify` prints no RLS section at all and a run citing it has not consulted this oracle

acceptance.clause: A's list contains exactly A's notes — none of B's (presence AND absence, from the server row set, not the UI)
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note as A: records[] titles include 'A note 1', exclude B's title; symmetric check as B

acceptance.clause: foreign by-id READ is denied server-side (non-2xx) — owner isolation holds at record granularity, not just list filtering
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<B's id> as A answers non-200 (403 PERMISSION_DENIED or a not-found-shaped denial — capture which; both are honest owner isolation, a 200 is the failure)

acceptance.clause: foreign by-id WRITE is denied and the row is unchanged (the #1994 'you can't mutate what you can't see' invariant)
acceptance.verify: PATCH as A answers >=400 AND the admin re-read of B's note shows the pre-attempt body — a 4xx with a mutated row is still a FAIL

acceptance.clause: admin (platform posture) reads the full set — the entitled side of the same gate (both sides, RUNNER rule 4 / ADR-0124 D5)
acceptance.verify: admin GET list contains every id created in this run

acceptance.clause: runRlsProofs reports rls-consistent (or member-visible on deliberately public objects) for every non-skipped showcase object; any rls-hole verdict is a FAIL and files an issue
acceptance.verify: run `objectstack verify --rls` (or runRlsProofs(stack, adminToken, memberToken, config) from packages/verify/src/rls.ts directly); summary.holes must be 0. A bare `objectstack verify` emits no PROVEN/HOLES line and cannot satisfy this clause

acceptance.clause: skipped objects in the verify report are each explainable (no plain-text probe field / blocked fixture) — a skip hiding a hole is the #3415 seed-defect class; this clause is ALSO the CANONICAL home of the standing expected-fail probe for the security-sensitive defect held privately under the handle D11 (#7463) — ⚠ NOT the public D11 row of FOLLOW-UPS.md §7c (the two-factor get-totp-uri re-reveal), an unrelated defect that later took the same number
acceptance.verify: for each status:'skipped' row, the detail names the benign reason; spot-check one skipped object by hand with the by-id read/write probe. ⚠ The D11 write-up was delivered to the maintainer PRIVATELY under the ruling recorded on #7463 (same handling as D1) and is deliberately not reproduced in this repo's FOLLOW-UPS.md, in run record #7637, or here — judge the spot-check against that private write-up and its private fix card, never tick this clause green over it, and never restate the defect in a public run issue
acceptance.evidence: report detail lines + the spot-check trace

negative: the foreign by-id write must not silently succeed: a 2xx on the forged PATCH, or a 4xx that still mutated the row (verified by the admin re-read), is a FAIL even though every list looked correctly filtered

the private D11 defect is recorded ONCE, here (acceptance[5], a run record's A6): access-security.owd-sharing-matrix clause 4 (acceptance[4], a run record's A5) reaches the same defect through the controlled_by_parent path and cross-references this clause, so a run carries the verdict on THIS item only — recording it on both double-counts one defect (#7687)

⚠ naming collision, never conflate them: the private handle D11 is unrelated to 'ADR-0090 D11', the external-OWD authoring clause cited by access-security.owd-save-gate, AND to the public D11 row of FOLLOW-UPS.md §7c (the two-factor get-totp-uri re-reveal) — three different things sharing one name. Cite this item and its clause, never the bare handle

source: #7637 (run record) — the by-id spot-check on a skipped object is where the private D11 defect surfaced
#7463 (maintainer ruling: the D11 write-up stays private, same handling as D1)

expanded to deep-test contract: concrete steps, multi-clause acceptance, negatives, variants

items.title: Write-path guards: readonly strip, owner_id forge/transfer denied, bulk validation
personas: admin

two non-admin members (owner forge is only meaningful non-privileged; everyone baseline grants private-note create/edit and contact is reachable read-only, so use a member with showcase_contributor where create is needed)

requires: showcase_contact.lead_score is the seeded readonly:true field (no defaultValue — stripped writes read back null)
showcase_private_note carries the owner_id anchor
showcase_invoice.tax_rate + line quantity/unit_price/product lock via readonlyWhen record/parent.status == 'paid'

steps: boot showcase isolated; admin session + two members Alice and Bob (fresh sign-ups — invite each one first — the stock showcase declares no auth.audience, so the invite_only default answers an uninvited POST /api/v1/auth/sign-up/email 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED; an admin POST /api/v1/auth/organization/invite-member for the address admits the sign-up (or admin POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user, which answers mustChangePassword:true)); resolve their sys_user ids via the data API or objectql

as admin (contact create is admin-side in the stock matrix): POST /api/v1/data/showcase_contact {"name": "RO probe", "email": "ro-probe@verify.test", "lead_score": 10} — forging the readonly field on INSERT; GET the row back
PATCH the same contact with {"lead_score": 99}; GET again

as Alice: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note {"title": "planted", "owner_id": "<Bob's id>"} (insert forge); then POST a note with {"owner_id": "<Alice's own id>"} (explicit self-owner); then PATCH her own note with {"owner_id": "<Bob's id>"} (transfer) and with {"owner_id": null} (disown)

as Alice: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/createMany with a BARE JSON ARRAY of 3 records carrying no owner_id (e.g. [{"title": "bulk 1"}, …]) — the body is the array itself; a {"records": […]} wrapper answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED ('the body must be a JSON array of record objects'); GET them back and read owner_id on each

as admin: set an invoice to status 'paid', then PATCH its tax_rate and a line's quantity — the readonlyWhen lock (#3042 bulk half: updateMany over a set including the paid invoice's line). updateMany is id-based: the body is {"records": [{"id": "<line id>", "data": {…}}, …]} — a {where, data} body answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED naming `records`

bulk-update a set where some rows violate a validation rule (e.g. showcase_invoice_line quantity below min 0 on some rows only) via POST /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice_line/updateMany {"records": [{"id", "data"}, …], "options": {"continueOnError": true}}; read the per-row outcome. ⚠️ Without options.continueOnError the bulk run stops at the FIRST failure (the BatchOptionsSchema default): rows before it are applied, the failing row carries its own error and every later row reports errors[0].code NOT_ATTEMPTED — so put a compliant row AFTER the violating one and send continueOnError true for the mixed-outcome leg; the default run is the stop-at-first-failure shape, also worth one capture

acceptance.clause: readonly field is stripped on INSERT — stored value is the default (null for lead_score), never the payload's; the create itself still succeeds (#3043 admit-and-strip, not reject)
acceptance.verify: POST answers 2xx; GET /api/v1/data/showcase_contact/<id> shows lead_score null; response header/body droppedFields advertises the strip (#3431)

acceptance.clause: readonly field is stripped on UPDATE — value unchanged after PATCH (#2948/#3003; note: a deployment opting into strictReadonlyWrites refuses instead with ERR_READONLY_FIELD_REJECTED per #5126 — stock showcase is strip)
acceptance.verify: before/after GETs identical on lead_score

acceptance.clause: owner forge on INSERT is DENIED for the member and the row is not created
acceptance.verify: POST with owner_id=<Bob> as Alice answers >=400; a system-context count of notes titled 'planted' is 0

acceptance.clause: owner transfer and disown on UPDATE are DENIED; owner unchanged — while explicit SELF-owner insert succeeds (the guard gates on identity, not on the key's presence)
acceptance.verify: PATCH owner_id=<Bob> and owner_id=null both >=400 with owner_id re-reading as Alice's id; POST with owner_id=<Alice's own id> is 2xx and persists

acceptance.clause: empty-owner bulk insert stamps the calling member on every row
acceptance.verify: all createMany rows read back owner_id == Alice's sys_user id

acceptance.clause: readonlyWhen locks hold at the API on the locked state: paid invoice's tax_rate and its lines' quantity/unit_price/product are not writable, and a bulk update is judged PER ROW — the locked field is dropped only from the rows whose own (or parent's) state locks it, reported on that row as results[i].droppedFields (reason readonly_when), while the same field on an unlocked row in the same batch is applied (#3042)
acceptance.verify: post-write reads show the locked fields unchanged on the paid invoice and its lines; in a mixed updateMany, the locked row's results[i].droppedFields names the field with reason readonly_when, the unlocked row carries none and re-reads changed

acceptance.clause: bulk update evaluates validation rules PER ROW (the #3106 updateMany gap must not reproduce): violating rows rejected/skipped, compliant rows applied — one mixed batch shows both outcomes
acceptance.verify: updateMany response distinguishes per-row results; re-reads confirm compliant rows changed and violating rows did not — measured with options.continueOnError true (rows before and after the violating one applied, the violating row VALIDATION_FAILED and unchanged); the default stop (later rows NOT_ATTEMPTED and unchanged) is a different shape and does not satisfy this clause on its own

negative: run the forge/transfer clauses as ADMIN too and confirm they SUCCEED where legitimately privileged — the guard must gate on privilege, not break the admin path (wrong-persona trap, both sides)

isSystem writes must still set readonly fields (A1's isSystem carve-out): verify via an objectql write with context {isSystem:true} that lead_score IS settable system-side. No REST door reaches an in-process isSystem write, by design, so score this from the two objectql pins `automated` names for it (the exemption is one engine function, gated on isSystem, for every object)

automated.ref: packages/qa/dogfood/test/owner-anchor-and-bulk-writes.dogfood.test.ts (+ showcase-static-readonly.dogfood.test.ts, showcase-readonly-when-parent.dogfood.test.ts); negative[1] (the isSystem exemption, which no REST door reaches by design) by packages/objectql/src/engine-insert-static-readonly-strip.test.ts ('isSystem seeds the readonly column — the exemption the ruling names', the INSERT path) + packages/objectql/src/engine-readonly-strip-caller-values.test.ts ('an isSystem caller is untouched by any of this', the UPDATE path on a static readonly column), both on a real engine

history.change: initial — merged from #3358 §9 and the 15.1 A-group rows these dogfood tests pin
expanded to deep-test contract: concrete steps, multi-clause acceptance, negatives, variants

checklist-accuracy findings of QA run #21056. acceptance[5] said a bulk update touching a locked row drops the field for the batch; updateMany runs engine.update per row with its own drop listener (metadata-protocol updateManyData), so only the locked row loses the field and the report is per row, results[i].droppedFields. steps[0] mints the members invite-first under the invite_only default

partial-coverage gap of QA run #21720 parked on #22017 (row 12). N2 was not runnable: there is no REST door for an in-process isSystem write, and no pin targeted it. Disposition: pin. engine-insert-static-readonly-strip.test.ts and engine-readonly-strip-caller-values.test.ts already prove the isSystem exemption on a real engine, on INSERT and UPDATE. `automated` names them for negative[1], and the negative says to score it from them

wire shapes the steps left out (#23878 checklist-accuracy findings, re-measured on main c91af8ed6). createMany takes a bare JSON array (a {records} wrapper answers 400 VALIDATION_FAILED); updateMany takes {records:[{id,data}]} (a where body answers 400 naming records); and a bulk run stops at the first validation failure by default, marking later rows NOT_ATTEMPTED, so clause 7's mixed-outcome step now sends options.continueOnError true. Measured on showcase_invoice_line [valid, quantity -1, valid]: default → succeeded 1, failed 2 (VALIDATION_FAILED, NOT_ATTEMPTED), only row 0 changed; continueOnError → succeeded 2, failed 1, rows 0 and 2 changed, row 1 unchanged

items.title: Record-grained access explain shows per-layer attribution and a verdict
personas: admin (drives the panel and the explain API)
auditor (viewAllRecords persona whose access is explained)
plain member (the deny case)

requires: a showcase_private_note owned by a third user (the probe record)
auditor member granted showcase_auditor (sys_user_permission_set row, as showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts does)

steps: boot showcase with the console; as admin create the probe: a member-owned showcase_private_note; grant a second member showcase_auditor

in the console's access explain panel — Studio's Access pillar (/_console/studio/PKG/access, e.g. com.example.showcase) → the header's 'Explain access' action (objectui packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AccessExplainPanel.tsx) — pick user = the auditor, object = showcase_private_note, record = the probe; screenshot the layered result
call the API twin: POST /api/v1/security/explain (client security.explain; GET variant also mounted — rest-route-ledger security-explain family) with the same user/object/record; capture the JSON
as the auditor (real session): GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<probe id> — the impersonated-read cross-check
repeat panel + API explain for the PLAIN member (no auditor set) on the same record
as the plain member: GET the same record and capture the denial

acceptance.clause: the panel attributes access per layer (permission set → position → sharing → row rules) and renders a record.visible verdict naming the deciding layer
acceptance.verify: screenshot shows all layers with the verdict

acceptance.clause: for the auditor the deciding layer is the VAMA bypass, attributed to the showcase_auditor set (explain() reports the vama_bypass layer — the permission-zoo pinned shape)
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/security/explain response names vama_bypass (or the equivalent layer key) with showcase_auditor as contributor

acceptance.clause: the explain verdict MATCHES the impersonated read, both ways: auditor verdict visible ∧ auditor GET 200; plain-member verdict not-visible ∧ plain-member GET non-200 (server truth outranks the panel)
acceptance.verify: compare record.visible against the actual GET status per persona — any disagreement is a FAIL against explain

acceptance.clause: the deny-side explain still answers 200 with a structured not-visible result naming the deciding layer — not EXPLAIN_FAILED, not an empty body
acceptance.verify: plain-member explain response: 200, visible=false, deciding layer named; error code EXPLAIN_FAILED absent

acceptance.clause: panel and API twin agree (same layers, same verdict) — the console must render the server's explanation, not recompute its own
acceptance.verify: field-by-field compare of the panel's displayed layers vs the POST /api/v1/security/explain body

negative: explain for the plain member must NOT show visible=true merely because the ADMIN is the one asking — the explanation is about the target user, not the caller (wrong-persona); cross-check with the plain member's own denied GET

items.title: A read-only package actually locks Studio editing surfaces
personas: admin

requires: the writable-package contrast side (step 5, acceptance clause 3) needs a writable BASE package: a scratch base created at runtime through POST /api/v1/packages, not a stock fixture. ⛔ Not POST /packages/:id/duplicate: requireDuplicableSource refuses a code-package source with 422 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE (#14451), and com.example.showcase is a code package

steps: boot showcase with the console; open Studio → object designer and the permission matrix on an object belonging to a read-only (installed/locked) package
screenshot the surface; then read the DOM state of the edit affordances (checkboxes, Save)
attempt the edit through the UI anyway (click a checkbox / Save) and capture what the client does
forge the write directly: PUT /api/v1/meta/object/<packaged object name> with a trivial field change, as the same admin session

POST /api/v1/packages to create a scratch writable base package — the manifest needs a `type` (e.g. {"manifest": {"id": "com.example.qa-base", "name": "QA Base", "version": "1.0.0", "scope": "project", "type": "app"}}; without it the install door answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming manifest.type, and scope must be one of cloud | system | project), author an object into it (PUT /api/v1/meta/object/<namespace>_<name>?package=<scratch id>, the namespace being the one the install echoes back) — the object needs a `sharingModel` (e.g. 'private'), or the save answers 422 INVALID_METADATA with rule security-owd-unset — then repeat the same trivial-change PUT against that object to prove the guard discriminates by package writability, not by blanket denial. ⛔ Do not duplicate com.example.showcase: POST /packages/com.example.showcase/duplicate answers 422 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE, because the source must be a base (#14451)

acceptance.clause: the read-only badge renders AND the controls are actually disabled — checkboxes/Save inert, edit affordances absent
acceptance.verify: after screenshot confirms render, assert disabled state on the controls (a badge alone is not a lock)

acceptance.clause: the SERVER refuses the same write: direct PUT /api/v1/meta/object/<name> on the read-only package answers 4xx with a ledgered metadata-protocol code (NOT_OVERRIDABLE for the bare PUT — object is not org-overridable; WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED, or ITEM_LOCKED for _lock'd items, when the write names ?package=) — UI absence never suffices (ADR-0124 D1)
acceptance.verify: PUT response status >=400 and error.code ∈ {NOT_OVERRIDABLE, WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED, ITEM_LOCKED} (packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, @objectstack/metadata-protocol entry) — record which spelling of the PUT produced which code

acceptance.clause: the same PUT against an object in a writable base package (created via POST /api/v1/packages — not duplicate, which refuses code sources per #14451) succeeds for the same admin and a follow-up GET shows the change.
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/packages creates the scratch base; the PUT on an object authored into it answers 2xx, and a follow-up GET shows the change
acceptance.evidence: the package-create, PUT and GET traces

acceptance.clause: the denied write leaves the packaged object byte-identical (persistence of the lock)
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/meta/object/<name> before/after the denied PUT — identical

negative: a UI that greys the controls while the direct PUT succeeds is a FAIL of this item even though the screenshot looks correct — record it as a server-guard gap, not a UI polish issue
source: packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts#requireDuplicableSource (POST /packages/:id/duplicate refuses a code-package source with 422 DUPLICATE_SOURCE_NOT_A_BASE, #14451 — so the writable contrast is a scratch base created through POST /api/v1/packages)
docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md §D4 ('clone a base into a new writable package')

items.title: CRUD × permission-set matrix: every access-matrix.json row holds — allowed verbs succeed, withheld verbs 403, VAMA bounded
personas: admin
one fresh member per permission set under test (set granted via a sys_user_permission_set row, as showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts does) — invited first, see steps[0]
a second member as the foreign-row owner

requires: examples/app-showcase/access-matrix.json — it IS the expectation table (45 permission-set × object rows, measured on main c91af8ed6: 41 showcase_* rows plus 4 showcase_field_ops_delegate × sys_* rows — sys_business_unit, sys_business_unit_member, sys_user, sys_user_position; the two delegate rows on the security-catalog objects left with #23222; recount from the file each run)
seeded permission sets showcase_contributor/manager/executive/auditor/ops/member_default/guest_portal/field_ops_delegate/client_liaison (security bootstrap)
knownGaps: every authenticated member ALSO holds the everyone baseline showcase_member_default additively (ADR-0090 D5) — the effective expectation per cell is the UNION of the tested set's row and the baseline's row for that object; compute the union before judging a cell, or a baseline-granted read will look like a matrix violation. Measured on the committed table: 9 of the 164 showcase_* cells (41 rows × 4 verbs at revision 4) are granted ONLY by the baseline (showcase_auditor and showcase_executive can CREATE an inquiry and create+edit a private note; guest_portal can READ an inquiry; showcase_manager and showcase_ops can CREATE an inquiry). showcase-crud-persona-matrix.dogfood.test.ts computes the union and asserts those 9 as allowed.

access-matrix.json is the APP's declared matrix; the platform's own baseline permission sets are additionally in force and grant some sys_* surface the app matrix never mentions (measured: a plain member reads /data/sys_user 200, self-scoped). So the absence of a row is NOT a prediction of denial on sys_* objects, and the automated sweep judges the showcase_* rows only — see automated.ref.

clause 5 (guest_portal create-without-read) is UNOBSERVABLE on a stock boot — record it blocked(fixture), never pass or fail. The guest anchor ships unbound (binding guest → showcase_guest_portal is an admin action; the app only ships the capability, permission-sets.ts GuestPortalPermissionSet), a member persona holding the set also holds the baseline's read on showcase_inquiry, and QA run #21056 measured REST anonymous create AND read both answering 401 even with the anchor bound. The only anonymous create lane is the public form (publicFormGrant on the inquiry form view, ADR-0056 Option A), whose grant is create plus read-back of the row it created — a different contract from this clause's

items.title: Sharing-model / OWD matrix: private, public_read, public_read_write, controlled_by_parent each enforce their declared baseline
personas: admin
members A and B (baseline only)
contributor members for the invoice/line and project cases
ops (modifyAllRecords contrast on announcements)
auditor (viewAllRecords contrast on lines)

requires: one seeded object per model, from the access-matrix sharingModel column: showcase_private_note (private), showcase_announcement (public_read), showcase_account + showcase_project (public_read_write), showcase_invoice_line under showcase_invoice (controlled_by_parent)
contributor invoice RLS owner == current_user.email (permission-sets.ts invoice_own_rows) — invoices must be created with owner set to the creating contributor's email

steps: boot showcase isolated; create members A and B (baseline), two contributor members C1/C2 (grant showcase_contributor), an ops member, an auditor member
private: as A create a showcase_private_note; as B list, GET by id, PATCH it
public_read: as admin (or ops) create a showcase_announcement owned by someone other than B; as B GET list + by id, then PATCH it; as ops PATCH the same announcement (modifyAllRecords contrast)

controlled_by_parent: as C1 POST /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice {"name": "INV-C1-1", "owner": "<C1 email>", "status": "draft"} then POST /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice_line {"invoice": <that id>, "product": <seeded product id>, "quantity": 1}; as C2 list lines, GET C1's line by id, PATCH it
as C1: GET/PATCH their OWN line by id (the entitled side of ADR-0055 derivation)
as auditor: list showcase_invoice_line — viewAllRecords crosses the derived scope
capture per-model, per-persona verb outcomes

acceptance.clause: private: only the owner reads/writes — B's list excludes A's note, B's by-id GET and PATCH are non-2xx, A's own read/write 2xx
acceptance.verify: the four traces; PATCH denial confirmed unchanged by admin re-read

acceptance.clause: public_read: everyone reads, only owner writes — B GET 200 (list and by id) but B PATCH >=400 with the row unchanged
acceptance.verify: B's GET/PATCH traces + admin re-read of the announcement

acceptance.clause: public_read: modifyAllRecords crosses the owner-writes baseline — ops' PATCH of the same foreign announcement is 2xx and persists (the bypass matters exactly where the baseline stops)
acceptance.verify: ops PATCH 2xx + re-read shows the change

acceptance.verify: both PATCH traces; the OWD opens records, never verbs the set withholds

acceptance.clause: controlled_by_parent: line access derives from the master (ADR-0055) — C2 cannot list, read by id, or PATCH C1's line (C1's invoice is outside C2's owner-RLS read set); C1 reads and writes their own line by id
acceptance.verify: C2's three denials (list excludes, by-id non-200, PATCH >=400 + unchanged) and C1's 2xx pair; no line-level rule is authored — derivation is the only mechanism in play. ⚠ DEDUPE: C2's by-id probes reach the SAME security-sensitive defect that access-security.rls-both-sides clause 5 (acceptance[5], a run record's A6) carries canonically under the private handle D11 — not FOLLOW-UPS.md §7c's public D11 row, an unrelated defect (#7463 ruling; nothing about it is described in this ledger, in run record #7637, or here). acceptance.verify: auditor list contains C1's line

acceptance.clause: all four model variants are exercised and each verdict is recorded per persona-verb — a model not driven leaves the item partial
acceptance.verify: run record carries verdicts for private / public_read / public_read_write / controlled_by_parent

items.title: Field-level security: editable:false strips/denies writes API-side and renders read-only in the UI; masked-read half needs an authored readable:false grant
personas: contributor (the FLS-restricted persona: showcase_project.budget/spent/budget_remaining readable:true, editable:false)
admin (the unrestricted contrast)

requires: showcase_contributor.fields FLS on showcase_project budget figures (permission-sets.ts — keys are <object>.<field> qualified; bare keys silently enforce nothing, the compile-time lint security-fls-unqualified-key guards that)
a seeded showcase_project row with a non-null budget

showcase_client_liaison — the STOCK readable:false grant since #9308 fixture 4 (permission-sets.ts): showcase_project { allowRead: true } plus fields { 'showcase_project.budget' | '.spent' | '.budget_remaining': { readable: false, editable: false } }, bound to the client_liaison position. Grant it to a FRESH member and to nobody who also holds showcase_contributor: field permissions merge most-permissive across the sets a caller holds, so contributor's readable:true would legitimately un-mask all three
knownGaps: [CLOSED — API half by #9481, the seed gap itself by #9308 fixture 4; the gap text stays because it carries the reason] stock showcase authored NO readable:false FLS grant, so the read-MASKING half (plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts) had no stock fixture and a run had to author a scratch permission set at runtime — which the SERVER half could do (showcase-fls-read-mask-strip.dogfood.test.ts does exactly that) but the UI half could not, because a console render cannot be driven off a permission set that exists only inside a test's stack. showcase_client_liaison is now that grant on stock seeds, so clause 5 is runnable end to end: grant the set to a fresh member, sign in as them, and compare their API body and their console render against the admin's. packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-client-liaison-fixtures.dogfood.test.ts pins the server half of the stock grant (by id, in lists, through an explicit $select) with the admin as the entitled contrast.

all three budget figures are withheld together, not just `budget` — `budget_remaining` is a formula over `budget - spent`, so masking one of the three leaks it back through arithmetic. A run that ticks clause 5 having observed only `budget` absent has not checked the mask that matters.

MASKED and STRIPPED are two different mechanisms with two different wire shapes, and this item's clause 4 ("absent or nulled") predates the measurement. Measured answer: a permission-set readable:false DELETES the key (strip); the #8993 `maskingRule` path REPLACES the value and leaves the key present (mask). A test that only checks "I did not get the real value" passes for both and pins neither, so the pin asserts key-absence. The masked half has no fixture at all — do not tick it off the strip pin.

steps: boot showcase with the console; contributor member (grant showcase_contributor); pick a seeded showcase_project and record its budget via a system-context read
as contributor over the API: PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_project/<id> {"name": "<name> (edited)"} — an editable field, then PATCH {"budget": 999999999} — the FLS-locked field
re-read the project system-side; compare budget before/after
as admin: PATCH the same budget field to a new value and re-read (the entitled side)

in the console as the contributor: open the project's detail/edit form; screenshot; inspect the state of the budget and spent controls — the two budget figures the edit form renders (project.view.ts form section 'Budget & Schedule': budget, spent, start_date, end_date). budget_remaining is a formula field and is not on the edit form at all

read-mask half (see knownGaps): grant the STOCK showcase_client_liaison set (fixtures.requires[2] — the readable:false grant on budget, spent and budget_remaining; no scratch set is needed) to a fresh member who holds no showcase_contributor, then GET the project as that member and inspect whether the masked field is absent/nulled in the API body AND blank in the UI render
as admin GET the same row — the unmasked contrast

acceptance.clause: editable field write succeeds for the contributor (the FLS lock is per-field, not per-object)
acceptance.verify: name PATCH 2xx and re-reads changed

acceptance.clause: editable:false field write is refused/stripped for the contributor and the stored value is unchanged (the permission-zoo pinned behavior: status >= 400 and budget identical)
acceptance.verify: budget PATCH answers >=400 (or a documented strip) AND the system-context re-read equals the pre-write budget — the value oracle decides, not the status alone

acceptance.clause: the SAME write succeeds for admin — the lock keys on the caller's FLS, not on the field (both sides)
acceptance.verify: admin budget PATCH 2xx + persisted re-read

acceptance.clause: the UI renders the FLS state faithfully for the contributor: the budget figures the edit form carries (budget and spent) are visible (readable:true) but not editable — input disabled/read-only on the edit form. budget_remaining is a formula: it is never on the edit form and never editable for anyone, so it cannot discriminate the FLS lock and is not scored here
acceptance.verify: after a screenshot confirms the form rendered, assert the disabled/read-only state of the budget and spent controls (the form section names exactly those two of the three figures, examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/project.view.ts); an EDITABLE budget or spent input for the contributor is the fail

acceptance.clause: read masking (given the scratch readable:false grant): the masked field is absent or nulled in the member's API read AND blank in their UI render, while admin's read carries the value — API and UI agree, both personas
acceptance.verify: member GET body lacks/nulls the field; admin GET carries it; UI screenshots per persona match their API bodies

negative: a UI-only lock is a FAIL: if the form disables the control but the direct PATCH mutates budget, record a server-guard gap (the API clause is the oracle, the DOM clause is corroboration only)

automated.ref: packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-permission-zoo.dogfood.test.ts (FLS budget case — WRITE half: the showcase's own readable:true/editable:false grant) + packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-fls-read-mask-strip.dogfood.test.ts (READ half, asserted server-side: a readable:false field is STRIPPED — the KEY is absent from the by-id record, from every listed row and from an explicit `select` that names it, and it is neither nulled nor replaced by a placeholder — while the entitled caller still receives it on the same row and request; filtering or sorting on the stripped field is refused 403 PERMISSION_DENIED naming the field, and the entitled caller can still do both; the read-deny's write complement is refused and the stored value is unchanged. The scratch readable:false set is authored at runtime, per this item's own steps). The read pin covers the STRIP mechanism only; do not read it as covering the masked one.

items.title: Scope depth (readScope/writeScope): org-wide read with own-only write, per persona — depth widens along geometry, never bypasses
personas: plain member M (creates the foreign probe inquiries via member_default create:true)
manager (readScope org / writeScope own on showcase_inquiry)
executive (readScope org, no write, on showcase_inquiry + showcase_private_note)
ops (readScope org / writeScope org on showcase_inquiry)

requires: showcase_inquiry is OWD private with create granted to the baseline — depth only matters where the baseline stops (permission-sets.ts docblock)
personas staffed by granting the sets (sys_user_permission_set) or assigning the positions manager/exec/ops (each declares its set in permissionSets, examples/app-showcase/src/security/positions.ts)
knownGaps: No permanent pin scores a clause of this item, so it carries no `automated` field and every clause is driven by hand. The three dogfood suites nearest to it, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth-write.dogfood.test.ts and packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth-fallback.dogfood.test.ts, assert the business-unit depth axis on showcase notes (readScope unit / unit_and_below / own_and_reports, writeScope unit, the absent-writeScope default, the fallback profile and the open edition's fail-closed degrade). None of them drives the manager / executive / ops personas or showcase_inquiry, so none asserts the org-read / own-write asymmetry acceptance[0]–[5] score. `automated` returns when a pin asserts one of those clauses in full

steps: boot showcase isolated; create member M plus manager/executive/ops personas; as M: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_inquiry {"name": "M probe", "email": "m.probe@example.com", "message": "scope probe"} (showcase_inquiry requires name, email and message and has no `subject` field — examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/inquiry.object.ts); as the manager: POST their OWN inquiry
as the manager: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_inquiry (list) — M's inquiry must appear (readScope org on a private object)
as the manager: PATCH M's inquiry (foreign write, writeScope own) and PATCH their own inquiry
as the executive: GET the inquiry list and M's inquiry by id; then attempt PATCH (no edit bit at all); also GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note list (readScope org over private notes)
as ops: PATCH M's inquiry (writeScope org)
as M: GET the manager's inquiry by id — the baseline member must NOT get org-wide read (the contrast that proves depth did the widening)
capture all traces + admin re-reads after every denied write

acceptance.clause: manager reads org-wide on the private object: M's inquiry present in the manager's list and readable by id
acceptance.verify: GET list contains 'M probe'; by-id GET 200

acceptance.clause: manager's write stays own-scoped (the read/write ASYMMETRY): PATCH on M's inquiry >=400 with the row unchanged; PATCH on the manager's own inquiry 2xx
acceptance.verify: both PATCH traces + admin re-read of M's inquiry

acceptance.clause: executive reads org-wide (inquiries AND private notes) but cannot write at all — every PATCH >=400, rows unchanged
acceptance.verify: list/by-id GETs 200 with foreign rows present; PATCH >=400 + unchanged re-read

acceptance.clause: ops writes org-wide: PATCH on M's inquiry 2xx and persisted (the entitled side of the exact guard that denied the manager)
acceptance.verify: ops PATCH 2xx + re-read shows the change

acceptance.clause: the baseline member has NO org-wide read: M cannot read the manager's inquiry by id and M's list holds only M's own — depth was the widener, not the object or route
acceptance.verify: M's by-id GET non-200; M's list excludes the manager's inquiry

acceptance.clause: each persona variant is driven and recorded (manager / executive / ops read+write outcomes) — the asymmetry table in the run record matches the readScope/writeScope columns of access-matrix.json

items.title: Criteria sharing rules widen the OWD baseline: matching rows become visible to the rule's audience, non-matching stay hidden
personas: a member in the rule's audience (position / unit_and_subordinates)
a member NOT in the audience
admin

requires: the shipped criteria sharing rules + sys_business_unit tree (examples/app-showcase/src/security/)

a runtime member added to the Field Operations business-unit subtree — as admin POST /api/v1/data/sys_business_unit_member {"user_id": "<member>", "business_unit_id": "bu_west_coast"} (a descendant of bu_field_ops) — as the unit audience, a member outside that subtree as the outsider, and a manager-position member only to record the position variant's depth confound (knownGaps)
knownGaps: the owner-based rule is [experimental] and skipped per the liveness ledger — exclude it; criteria + position/unit audiences are the live surface

the POSITION-audience variant is CONFOUNDED on stock and scores no widening clause. The only seeded position rule, share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers, shares Northwind-qualified showcase_contact rows with the manager position, and manager's showcase_manager set reads showcase_contact at readScope 'org'. Measured on main c91af8ed6: a manager-holding member reads all 32 contacts, and POST /api/v1/security/explain answers visible, decidedBy 'depth' on a matching AND a non-matching contact — the sharing layer never decides. So acceptance[0]-[2] are scored on the unit_and_subordinates variant (share_new_inquiries_with_field_ops: a member of bu_field_ops or a descendant unit reads exactly the status='new' inquiry, and its sys_record_share row carries source 'rule'); the position variant records its depth-decided reads as the confound. A position audience without org depth is authored in-run by access-security.sharing-rule-authoring-ui

variants: criteria rule, position audience (confounded on stock by showcase_manager's org-depth read — see knownGaps; recorded, not scored as widening)
manual one-off share via the record-shares route
steps: boot the showcase on its own port and file DB (dogfood §0's isolation, RUNNER's canonical boot line) in the stock `single` tenancy posture: no clause needs OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated or any walled boot; add the audience member to bu_west_coast through sys_business_unit_member (fixtures.requires); give a second member the manager position to record the position confound

the probes are seeded: share_new_inquiries_with_field_ops matches status='new', and the seed ships one new, one contacted and one closed showcase_inquiry (OWD private). Use the new one as the MATCHING probe and a non-new one as the NON-MATCHING probe
as the audience member: GET the object list and GET each probe by id
as a member OUTSIDE the audience: same reads
read sys_record_share for the matching record; run /security/explain for the audience member + matching record

manual-share the non-matching inquiry to a specific user via the record-shares route (POST /api/v1/data/showcase_inquiry/<id>/shares); that user re-reads, and a third member re-reads too. The recipient needs object-level read on the object: a share on showcase_contact to a baseline member lands 201 but the member's read answers 403 at the object gate, because the member baseline grants no showcase_contact read — so a manual share is only observable on an object the recipient can already read at object level

§A13: as admin switch the DECLARED rule off at the activation door — POST /api/v1/security/_activation/sharing_rule/share_new_inquiries_with_field_ops {"enabled": false}; re-read the audience member's list and by-id read of the matching inquiry, the rule-sourced sys_record_share rows and the sys_metadata_activation row; restart the server on the same database and re-read; switch it back on ({"enabled": true}), re-read, restart once more and re-read. There is no seeded sys_sharing_rule row to edit any more: declared rules are read from the registry (ADR-0131 D2, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts) and GET /api/v1/data/sys_sharing_rule answers total 0 on stock, so the activation switch is the administrator's durable artifact. The materialized share is not editable: PATCH /api/v1/data/sys_record_share/<id> answers 405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED (allowed get, list, aggregate, search, export)

acceptance.clause: the audience member reads the MATCHING record (list + by-id) though the object OWD is private — the rule widened access
acceptance.verify: audience member's list contains the matching id and the by-id GET is 200

acceptance.clause: the NON-matching record stays invisible to the same audience member, and the matching record stays invisible to a member outside the audience — widening is scoped, both sides
acceptance.verify: non-matching by-id GET is denied for the audience member; matching by-id GET is denied for the outsider

acceptance.clause: the widening is materialized: a sys_record_share row exists for the matching record and the explain output names the SHARING layer as the deciding grant (not OWD, not position)
acceptance.verify: sys_record_share read + /security/explain attribution

acceptance.clause: a manual one-off share grants exactly the target user and no one else (both sides)
acceptance.verify: target reads the record; a third user still cannot

acceptance.clause: §A13 — an administrator's switch on a DECLARED sharing rule survives a restart and is never undone by the boot: switched off at the activation door, share_new_inquiries_with_field_ops withdraws its grant (the audience member is denied, its rule-sourced sys_record_share row is gone, sys_metadata_activation reads active false); a cold restart on the same database leaves it off — the boot neither re-arms it nor re-materializes the grant; switched back on it restores exactly one rule-sourced share, which a second restart keeps. The declared rule is code with no stored row (ADR-0131 D2), so the ledger row IS the administrator's edit; sys_record_share refuses edits (405)
acceptance.verify: per stage — baseline, off, restart, on, restart — the audience member's list + by-id read of the matching inquiry, the outsider's read, the sys_record_share rows with source 'rule' for the rule (none while off, exactly one while on, the same id after the second restart), and the sys_metadata_activation row (active false/true, updated_at unchanged across each restart). ⛔ GET /api/v1/meta/sharing_rule/NAME keeps answering active: true while the ledger holds the rule off — that read is the DECLARATION, not the effective state, so it is never this clause's oracle
acceptance.evidence: the five-stage read table (member, outsider, share rows, ledger row)

negative: a non-matching record becoming visible to the audience (over-broad rule), or a matching record leaking to an outsider, is a FAIL; a share silently dropped on restart is the #2909 regression

history.change: initial — THE marquee gap: sharing rules (criteria → materialized sys_record_share) had zero behavioral coverage though showcase ships stock fixtures; owd-sharing-matrix only did baselines

re-pointed on main c91af8ed6 (#23878 checklist-accuracy findings). (1) The position-audience variant is confounded on stock: the manager position binds showcase_manager, which reads showcase_contact at readScope 'org', so a manager reads all 32 contacts and explain answers decidedBy 'depth' on matching and non-matching rows alike. A knownGap records it, the variant is marked recorded-not-scored, and the widening clauses are scored on the unit_and_subordinates rule (measured: a member added to bu_west_coast reads exactly the one status='new' inquiry, rule-sourced share row). Steps 1-2 name the provisioning and the seeded probes instead of the retired red-project example. (2) Step 7 / clause 5 (§A13) said 'edit a materialized share', but sys_record_share answers 405 to PATCH; the editable seeded artifact is the sys_sharing_rule row. (3) Step 6 records that a manual-share recipient needs object-level read (a contact share to a baseline member reads 403)

steps[6] and acceptance[4] (clause, verify, evidence) re-pointed — a checklist-accuracy finding of the 18.0 QA sweep (QA run #24559, access-security.sharing-rules-widen acceptance[4]; wave anchor #24579 §3) with its oracle from round 2 (QA run #24601). §A13 asked that an admin edit to the SEEDED sys_sharing_rule row survive a restart; the seeder that copied declared rules into that table is retired (ADR-0131 D2, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts) and GET /api/v1/data/sys_sharing_rule answers total 0, so there is no seeded row to edit. The administrator's durable act on a declared rule is now the activation switch (POST /api/v1/security/_activation/sharing_rule/NAME), and the clause asserts that switch across two restarts. QA run #24601 drove exactly this recipe at ba4afcc2 and passed. It measured that GET /api/v1/meta/sharing_rule/NAME keeps reading active: true while the ledger holds the rule off, so the oracle is the ledger row and the member's reads, never the metadata read. acceptance[0]–[3] are unchanged

steps[0] spells out its boot — checklist-accuracy finding of QA run #24779 (wave anchor #24579 round 12): the runner read 'boot showcase isolated' as the isolated tenancy posture, which no clause needs (all six passed on stock single). The ledger's 'isolated' boot is dogfood §0's own port and DB; the step now says that, and names the stock single posture. No clause changed

items.title: Per-record manual shares grant, scope, and revoke access on a private-OWD record; rule evaluate reconciles the audience
personas: member A (owner of the private-OWD probe note)
member B (the grantee — baseline only, no relation to A)
member C (a third baseline member — the isolation contrast)
admin (drives the rule evaluate + system-context re-reads)

requires: showcase_private_note (sharingModel: private — member_default grants create/read/edit, so a non-owner sees nothing without a share)
three fresh sign-ups (A/B/C) whose sys_user ids are resolved via a system-context read

the seeded criteria sharing rule share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers on showcase_contact (OWD private) + at least one qualified contact at company Northwind — seeded as Nora West (examples/app-showcase/src/security/sharing-rules.ts) — for the evaluate clause

a holder of the manager position, so the rule's recipient expansion is non-empty. Since #9237 the STOCK boot already satisfies this — the seeded dev admin holds manager (sys_user_position usp_showcase_admin_manager) and the boot backfill materialises the grant — so an evaluate with no extra assignment answers grantsCreated 0 out of IDEMPOTENCE, not emptiness. Read the gap off expandedUsers/matchedRecords, and assign the position to one more persona so a created grant is observable

steps: boot showcase isolated (own port + file DB, dogfood skill §0); admin session + members A/B/C (fresh emails); resolve their sys_user ids system-side
as A: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note {"title": "A share probe"} — capture the id; POST a SECOND note as A too (the revoke-scope probe below needs a different record id under the same object)
as B: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id> — the PRE-grant baseline (private OWD, B is not owner → must be refused)
as A: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id>/shares {"recipientType": "user", "recipientId": "<B id>", "accessLevel": "read"} — capture the 201 sys_record_share row (source 'manual')
as B: GET the note by id AND GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note (list) — the grant must make it visible both ways
as C: GET the note by id — still refused (the grant named B, not everyone)
as A: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id>/shares (management-gated list) — the manual grant is present
as B (a non-manager on A's note): POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id>/shares granting themselves — must be refused (creating a share is not a reader's power, ADR-0111 D5)

revoke-scope probe — run it BEFORE the real revoke, while the share still EXISTS: attempt DELETE of the shareId through the SECOND note's path (/data/showcase_private_note/<A second id>/shares/<shareId>) — must be refused (the URL's object/id is the revoke scope, ADR-0111 D4) AND the share must survive the attempt. Ordered after the revoke it proves nothing: the shareId no longer exists by then, so the same refusal comes back for a share that is simply gone
as A: DELETE /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id>/shares/<shareId> → 204; then as B: GET the note by id again — refused once more

as admin: assign the manager position to one persona (Setup -> Access Control), then POST /api/v1/sharing/rules/share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers/evaluate — capture the reconcile result; read sys_record_share for the matched contact

acceptance.clause: PRE-grant isolation holds: B's by-id GET of A's private note is non-2xx before any share exists (the baseline the grant then widens)
acceptance.verify: GET /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id> as B answers non-200 (403 PERMISSION_DENIED or a not-found-shaped denial) BEFORE the POST /shares

acceptance.clause: the manual grant lands as a sys_record_share row: POST .../shares answers 201 with recipient_type 'user', recipient_id B, access_level 'read', source 'manual', granted_by A
acceptance.verify: POST /api/v1/data/showcase_private_note/<A id>/shares status 201; the returned/re-read sys_record_share row carries those fields (packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-record-share.object.ts)
acceptance.evidence: the POST response + a system-context sys_record_share read

acceptance.clause: the grant widens B's read BOTH ways and stays scoped: after the grant B reads the note by id (200) AND it appears in B's list, while C (ungranted) still cannot read it by id
acceptance.verify: B by-id GET 200 + B list contains the id; C by-id GET non-200 and C list excludes it
acceptance.evidence: B's two reads + C's two reads

acceptance.clause: the shares list is management-gated: A (owner/manager) lists the record's shares, but B (visible-but-not-manager) POSTing a share is refused 403 (or 404 when the record is invisible) — reading a record does not confer re-share authority (ADR-0111 D5)
acceptance.verify: A GET .../shares 200 with the grant present; B POST .../shares >=400 (403 visible-not-manager / 404 invisible)

acceptance.clause: revoke retracts access: DELETE .../shares/:shareId answers 204 and B's next by-id GET is non-2xx again — access tracks the grant lifecycle, not a cached decision
acceptance.verify: DELETE 204; B by-id GET after revoke non-200; a system-context sys_record_share read shows the row gone

acceptance.clause: revoke is record-scoped: revoking the share id through a different record's path is refused — a share can only be revoked through the record it belongs to (ADR-0111 D4)
acceptance.verify: DELETE /data/showcase_private_note/<other id>/shares/<shareId> answers >=400 and the share still exists (re-read)
acceptance.evidence: the mis-scoped DELETE trace + survival read

acceptance.clause: rule evaluate reconciles the audience: POST /sharing/rules/share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers/evaluate returns {ruleId, matchedRecords>=1, grantsCreated/grantsUpdated} and a sys_record_share row exists for the matched contact with source 'rule' and source_id = the rule's id. For this DECLARED rule that id IS its name — a declared rule is projected from the registry, not stored, and its id is its name (ADR-0131 D2) — while an organization-authored rule's id is its sys_sharing_rule row id (srule_…)
acceptance.verify: the SharingRuleEvaluationResult body (packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts evaluateRule) + the materialized rule-sourced share row: assert share.source_id === the body's ruleId, which for this rule is 'share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers' (packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts#projectDeclaredRule projects a declared rule with id = name, and that id is what its grants carry as sys_record_share.source_id). The rule id is the stable key the reconcile path relies on — revokeRuleGrants(ruleId) purges where {source:'rule', source_id: ruleId}. ⛔ Do not look for a sys_sharing_rule row for this rule: that table holds only organization-authored rules and answers total 0 on stock
acceptance.evidence: evaluate response + the sys_record_share read (the row's source_id beside the body's ruleId)

negative: a revoked share whose record still reads 200 for B, or a grant that leaks to C, is a FAIL even though the manual grant looked correct — access must equal the live grant set
a non-manager (B) successfully POSTing a share on A's note is the ADR-0111 D5 authority gap — a 2xx there is a FAIL
source: packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts#REST_ROUTE_LEDGER (record-shares family: GET/POST /data/:object/:id/shares, DELETE .../:shareId; sharing-rules family evaluate — re-pointed #18104: shareId is a route PATH PARAMETER, carried in this file only inside a route string)

packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts#registerSharingEndpoints (the record-shares family: GET and POST /data/:object/:id/shares and DELETE .../:shareId, the body of RestServer#registerSharingEndpoints moved into this module whole) + packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts#registerSharingRuleEndpoints (the evaluate leg). The registerRecordShareEndpoints an older revision named still does not exist (#13788); the family's registrar is registerSharingEndpoints

history.change: new — per-record manual share grant/scope/revoke lifecycle on showcase_private_note plus rule-evaluate reconcile, grounded in the ADR-0111 record-shares routes

clause 6 text corrected against the implementation (run #7637): a rule-materialized share carries source_id = the sys_sharing_rule ROW ID, not the rule name — the stable FK purgeRuleGrants reconciles on. Semantic intent was already right; the asserted value was not

the evaluate clause was UNRUNNABLE as written and had been since it was authored: it drove share_red_projects_with_execs, a rule on showcase_project, whose public_read_write OWD leaves sharing nothing to widen — so evaluate's reconcile hit assertNotInertGrant and the call was refused (SHARING_NOT_ENABLED, ADR-0111 D7) rather than returning a reconcile result. That rule is retired; the clause now drives share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers on showcase_contact (OWD private), and a step assigns the manager position so the recipient expansion is non-empty

steps only — the revoke-scope probe was ordered AFTER the real revoke, which left clause 6's own evidence requirement ('the share still exists (re-read)') unsatisfiable for anyone following the steps literally: the shareId is already gone, so the refusal observed is the ordinary missing-share 404 and says nothing about record scoping. The probe now runs BEFORE the revoke, and the note-creation step creates the second record it needs. No acceptance clause changed. Found by the FIRST execution of this item, at revision 3

source[1] re-pointed (carried reading of the #23878 wave, confirmed on main c91af8ed6): it said the record-shares family is 'registered inline, under no registrar of its own'. packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts exports registerSharingEndpoints, which registers GET and POST /data/:object/:id/shares and DELETE .../:shareId; the evaluate leg stays on registerSharingRuleEndpoints. Anchor and wording only: no step, fixture or oracle changed, so no re-run is owed

acceptance[6] (clause, verify, evidence) corrected — a checklist-accuracy finding of the 18.0 QA sweep (QA run #24559, access-security.record-share-grant-revoke acceptance[6]; wave anchor #24579 §3). The clause required source_id to be the rule's sys_sharing_rule ROW id and NOT its name; that holds only for an organization-authored rule. The rule it evaluates, share_key_account_qualified_contacts_with_managers, is DECLARED, and a declared rule is projected with id = name (sharing-rule-service.ts projectDeclaredRule, ADR-0131 D2), so its grants carry the name. The clause now asserts source_id equals the rule's id as evaluate reports it, and the verify names revokeRuleGrants, the current name of the purge it cited as purgeRuleGrants

items.title: The audit-log browser surfaces attributable events over sys_audit_log with correct actor/object, filters, and a before/after payload drawer
personas: admin (drives the /system/audit-log page and the delete + settings write)
a fresh member (generates the attributable login event)

requires: sys_audit_log (plugin-audit; enable.apiMethods = get + list only — writes happen only through internal system hooks)
the console audit-log page at /system/audit-log (objectui apps/console/src/pages/system/AuditLogPage.tsx → /api/v1/data/sys_audit_log)
a deletable seeded record (e.g. a showcase_task) and a writable settings namespace for the config_change event

steps: boot showcase with the console; admin session

generate 3 attributable events with distinct action/actor/object: (a) a fresh member SIGNS IN (action 'login', actor = the member); (b) as admin DELETE a showcase_task via /api/v1/data/showcase_task/<id> (action 'delete', object_name showcase_task, record_id set); (c) write a setting (action 'config_change')
open /system/audit-log; wait for the table to settle; screenshot
locate all three events in the page and read their action / object / actor cells

narrow to writes and confirm the narrowing is server-side; capture the re-issued /api/v1/data/sys_audit_log request with its $filter. /system/audit-log (AuditLogPage) has an Action select in its filter bar that writes action into the request's $filter. The page's Presets row offers sys_audit_log's list views (Writes / Auth / Config / …), and its 'Open as list' link opens the sys_audit_log object list (no longer a Setup menu entry), which offers the same views and the generic Filter Records → Where → Add filter builder. Any of these is a valid server-side narrowing

items.title: OWD save gate: the retired external dial is refused on every object write, and a packaged object's OWD cannot be changed at runtime — the managed-content seal refuses the write before any OWD rule judges it — server-side
personas: admin (drives the direct meta PUTs)

requires: a writable/draft object name for the server probe (author via PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_owd_probe?mode=draft — no shipped object is mutated)
the showcase's shipped objects showcase_announcement and showcase_account, neither of which declares externalSharingModel
knownGaps: there is no external OWD to test: externalSharingModel was removed (ADR-0049) and the object schema refuses it at parse with the prescription "delete the key"; an external principal reaches explicitly shared rows only (the ADR-0095 EXTERNAL rung, never OWD-derived). This item tests the save gate (the retired key refused at write; a packaged object sealed against runtime change), NOT external-principal enforcement; do not tick an external-principal read/write result

R1 (owd_widening_forbidden) is UNREACHABLE through the metadata door on a stock deploy, and with OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object too. saveMetaItem asks the package door (refusePackagedBaseOverride, predicate isSealedManagedItem: the item is artifact-backed and `object` opens no overlay channel) on every kernel topology, ahead of the runtime lint door and the plugin-security authoring gate (#22338). Since ADR-0131 D6 (#22401) the escape hatch no longer opens an item a managed package ships. So any OWD write onto showcase_announcement is refused 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE (no ?package=) or 403 ITEM_LOCKED (?package= names the read-only base), whatever its direction: widening or tightening, hatch open or shut. The revision-3 reading, measured at #9477, no longer holds: a widening body met R1 first and answered 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with declaredCode owd_widening_forbidden, and a tightened control passed R1 and met NOT_OVERRIDABLE, or 2xx under OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object. R1 keeps its oracle in unit pins: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-posture-gate.test.ts for its verdict, and packages/rest/src/meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts for the door order that now puts the seal in front of it. ⛔ Do not build a fixture package only to reach R1 live (#23121 triage). If a run does see the R1 refusal on some other door, read the code from `declaredCode` (owd_widening_forbidden), not `code`: the wire `code` is PERMISSION_DENIED

steps: boot showcase with the console; admin session

server reject: PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_owd_probe with sharingModel:'private' + externalSharingModel:'private' — capture the 4xx + error code and the issue at externalSharingModel. Drive it at the active-state door AND at ?mode=draft: the refusal is the object schema's tombstone, which runs before the draft discipline defers any lint rule
server admit: PUT the same object without externalSharingModel — capture the 2xx (the refusal keys on the retired key, not on the OWD)

packaged object (the seal): PUT /api/v1/meta/object/showcase_announcement widening its shipped sharingModel public_read→public_read_write. Capture the 4xx AND its code. Expect 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE from the managed-content seal (saveMetaItem's package door, ADR-0131 D6), on a stock deploy and under OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=object alike. With ?package=com.example.showcase the same door answers 403 ITEM_LOCKED. Control leg, to show that the seal answers and not a direction-keyed gate: re-PUT the same body TIGHTENED (public_read→private). It is refused the same way, because a managed item is sealed whatever the body says. R1 (owd_widening_forbidden) is not reached on this door; clause 3 names its unit pins
GET /api/v1/meta/object/showcase_announcement before and after the denied PUT — confirm byte-identical
cross-check the shipped declarations: GET /api/v1/meta/object/showcase_account and showcase_announcement — neither carries externalSharingModel

acceptance.clause: the server refuses the retired externalSharingModel on ANY object write, draft included: the writable-object PUT carrying it answers 422 INVALID_METADATA with one issue at externalSharingModel carrying the prescription ("`object.externalSharingModel` was removed in @objectstack/spec 18 … Delete the key."), and nothing is stored
acceptance.verify: PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_owd_probe (active state, and again with ?mode=draft) answers 422 with code INVALID_METADATA, the issue path names externalSharingModel and its message carries the prescription; a follow-up GET finds no qa_owd_probe. ⛔ security-external-wider-than-internal and 403 owd_external_wider are both RETIRED spellings: the lint rule left with the key, and object-posture-gate.ts R2 was retired by the maintainer ruling on #8310
acceptance.evidence: the two PUT traces + the read

acceptance.clause: the server admits the same object without the key: the PUT with only sharingModel saves 2xx — the refusal keys on the retired key, not on the posture
acceptance.verify: PUT without externalSharingModel answers 2xx and a follow-up GET shows sharingModel and no externalSharingModel

acceptance.clause: a packaged object's OWD cannot be changed at runtime: the widening PUT on showcase_announcement is refused 403 with a ledgered code, recorded with WHICH layer answered. On a stock deploy that is 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE from the managed-content seal, saveMetaItem's package door (ADR-0131 D6, #22401). It answers ahead of every check that judges the body, on every kernel topology (#22338), and OS_METADATA_WRITABLE does not open it. So the plugin-security R1 gate (owd_widening_forbidden) is unreachable here on stock, and R1's oracle is its unit pins, not this run
acceptance.verify: PUT /api/v1/meta/object/showcase_announcement (widened, no ?package=) answers 403 with code NOT_OVERRIDABLE and no declaredCode; with ?package=com.example.showcase, which names the read-only base, the same door answers 403 ITEM_LOCKED. Either way the answering layer is the package door, not R1. The door order is pinned by packages/rest/src/meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts (the '[#7674] R1 owd_widening_forbidden through PUT /api/v1/meta/object/:name' block: a widening overlay of a packaged object answers 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE with no declaredCode and stores nothing, hatch open). R1's own verdict is pinned in-process by packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-posture-gate.test.ts (the 'R1 — env-tighten-only over a packaged declaration (ADR-0086 D1)' block). Cite both pins per rule 6 for R1; do not build a fixture package to reach it live
acceptance.evidence: the PUT trace + the code + the answering-layer note (+ the two cited pin outputs for R1)

acceptance.clause: the denied widening is inert: GET /api/v1/meta/object/showcase_announcement is byte-identical before and after the refused PUT
acceptance.verify: the two metadata reads match on sharingModel

acceptance.clause: the shipped app carries no retired key: showcase_account and showcase_announcement declare sharingModel and no externalSharingModel
acceptance.verify: GET both objects' metadata; each carries sharingModel and neither carries externalSharingModel

negative: a Studio panel that greys the save while a direct meta PUT widens is a FAIL — the server gate is the authority (ADR-0124 D1 both-sides)
a stock-deploy packaged-object widening PUT that answers 2xx (or leaves the object widened) is a FAIL
do NOT tick external-principal read/write enforcement: an external principal reaches explicitly shared rows only (ADR-0095) — this item is the save/authoring gate only
variants: the retired externalSharingModel (the object schema's tombstone, all object writes, draft included)
the managed-content seal (packaged/artifact-backed objects: 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE, or ITEM_LOCKED with ?package=, ahead of R1); R1 env-tighten-only is unreachable on this door and unit-pinned
source: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts#refusePackagedBaseOverride (saveMetaItem's package door — the managed-content seal: isSealedManagedItem, 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE, or ITEM_LOCKED for a named read-only base; asked on every kernel topology ahead of the body checks since #22338, and not opened by OS_METADATA_WRITABLE since ADR-0131 D6, #22401)

packages/rest/src/meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts (the door-order pin: a packaged object's overlay is refused by the package door before the lint door and R1, hatch open) + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/object-posture-gate.test.ts (R1's in-process unit pins)

history.change: new — OWD save gate both-sides: Studio inline external-wider warning + server object-posture-gate (R2 external≤internal on every write, R1 packaged tighten-only); external-principal evaluation carried as a knownGap (#2696 planned)

corrected clauses 1-2 and steps 2-3 for the #8310 retirement (maintainer ruling 2026-08-13). The item tested R2 owd_external_wider / 403 at the ?mode=draft door; R2 is RETIRED from object-posture-gate.ts as a duplicate of the runtime lint door, whose refusal is 422 INVALID_METADATA rule security-external-wider-than-internal raised at the ACTIVE-state door — and draft saves deliberately defer to the draft-to-active promotion gate (#4463 D1), so the clause was unobservable where it was pointed (#9453 CF-2). ⚠️ #9453 CF-3 (that the R1 knownGap mispredicts which layer answers) was NOT applied: object-posture-gate.ts states verbatim that R1 applies only to overlay writes over an artifact-backed object and that 'the default deploy already 403s these before this gate runs' (if (!ctx.isArtifactBacked) return), which is what the knownGap and clause 4 already say

the R1 knownGap, step 5 and clause 4 named the WRONG answering layer, and #9453 CF-3 was RIGHT — re-measured on a genuinely stock showcase boot and OVERTURNING the revision-2 note above (#9477). Proven stock from the server process's own /proc/<pid>/environ: zero METADATA_WRITABLE occurrences among 147 vars. Target artifact-backed, proven by GET ?layers=true returning a populated `code` layer (_packageId com.example.showcase) with `overlay: null`. A widening PUT then answered 403 declaredCode owd_widening_forbidden — reproduced twice, object byte-identical after. The mechanism the old text missed: saveMetaItem runs runAuthoringGate BEFORE the overlay/package doors on the host-config kernel the showcase boots (environmentId undefined, so protocol.ts's env-partitioned NOT_OVERRIDABLE branch never arms — the #7674 note in that file says the showcase is exactly that shape). So the deploy posture does not select the layer; the body's DIRECTION does. Control leg (same boot, same object, tightened body) passed R1 and answered 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE, i.e. the door the knownGap called 'earlier' is in fact LATER. Six legs measured (widen/tighten x stock/hatch x ?package= present/absent) and WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED appeared on none. ⛔ Not a product defect: every widening leg refused and the object never changed — object-posture-gate.ts behaved exactly as its executable guard (if (!ctx.isArtifactBacked) return) specifies; only the prose parenthetical in that file's header, and this item, mispredicted the door order

clause 4, acceptance[3], re-pointed to the managed-content seal, with step 5, the R1 knownGap, the first knownGap's packaged tighten-only parenthetical, the R1 variant, the title and two new source notes (stale spec, #23104 A3). Revision 3 measured, at #9477, that a widening PUT on showcase_announcement met R1 first and answered 403 PERMISSION_DENIED with declaredCode owd_widening_forbidden. Two later changes reorder that. #22338 made saveMetaItem ask the package door on every kernel topology, ahead of the checks that judge the body. ADR-0131 D6 (#22401, e02833c24) made the OS_METADATA_WRITABLE hatch stop opening an item a managed package ships. A packaged object, whose type opens no overlay channel, is now refused 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE (ITEM_LOCKED with ?package=) whatever the body says, so R1 is unreachable on this door on stock. The protection holds: nothing widens. Per the #23121 triage, no fixture package is built to reach R1. Its oracle is its unit pins, named in the clause: plugin-security object-posture-gate.test.ts for the verdict, and rest meta-object-owd-gate.test.ts, whose R1 block now pins the package door answering first, hatch open

the external clauses retired with the key (#23268, ruling of record 6159300530, letter A): externalSharingModel was removed from the object schema (ADR-0049), so the Studio external-wider clause goes and the external-wider refusal, admit and shipped-declarations clauses and the D11 knownGap are rewritten: clause 1 now asserts the tombstone's 422 refusal on every object write, draft included, clause 2 the admit without the key, and the last clause that the showcase ships no retired key. The packaged-object seal clauses are unchanged (the seal is now clause 3, and step 4 names it so). surface mixed → api: no browser step remains

items.title: A public form's withdrawal holds across the layers of the environment's definition: an administrator's save is environment-wide whatever organization is active and its withdrawal closes the form, a withdrawal in any package's body of the view name closes it in every package, only an explicit false withdraws, a package's shipped false withdraws, and the package-less environment-wide copy may open a form a package ships closed
personas: anonymous (no Authorization header, no cookie) on both public form doors, GET /api/v1/forms/:slug and POST /api/v1/forms/:slug/submit

platform admin (the seeded admin), saving the form from a session whose active organization is the Default Organization. Since ADR-0131 D6 that save is environment-wide, so the active organization is a premise the item holds, not a second layer it writes

requires: the stock public form: examples/app-showcase/src/ui/views/inquiry.view.ts#InquiryViews, formViews.contact (enabled and allowAnonymous true, publicLink '/forms/contact-us'), served as the flattened view item showcase_inquiry.contact with its sharing at config.sharing

the stock single tenancy posture and its Default Organization, whose owner is the seeded admin (packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/ensure-default-organization.ts#ensureDefaultOrganization). The admin makes it active with POST /api/v1/auth/organization/set-active, and an anonymous submission lands in it. Under a walled posture the stock form is not offered at all, because its object cannot take an anonymous submission there (packages/metadata-core/src/anonymous-form-intake.ts#anonymousFormIntakeUnavailability; packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-public-form-walled-intake.dogfood.test.ts and public-form-withdrawal-walled.dogfood.test.ts own that half): out of this item
